subject: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting

Neha,

We’re scoping the internal Console “Ops / Incidents” views that will sit alongside the new taxonomy rollout (PM-912 + ENG-4827). To avoid rework, can you confirm what incident metadata fields we should treat as canonical + required (vs optional) for dashboards and reporting?

What Console needs (v1):
- Filter/group incidents by category + impacted surface, plus owner/team
- Slice by region and deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private where Redwood is operator)
- Show time-to-mitigate (TTM) and time-to-resolve (TTR) rollups by category/owner
- Basic linkage out to the source-of-truth incident + postmortem

Concrete questions:
1) Which fields are required at incident declaration vs allowed to be set/edited post-incident?
2) Allowed values: should Console enforce allowed values (dropdowns) or rely on incident-bot validation?
3) For “impacted surface,” do we want both product surface (API/Console/Dedicated/Private) and technical surface (routing/runtime/fleet/etc.), or just one in v1?
4) What are the minimal identifiers we can display/link (e.g., incident ID, Slack channel, postmortem doc link)?

If there’s a current draft spec for “incident-metadata-standard” you’d like us to align to, please point me at it. We’re trying to lock UI requirements by next Wed to stay on track for the sprint.

Thanks,
Marissa
Product (Console + Platform UX)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting

Marissa — yep, good timing.

Canonical spec we’re converging on (Confluence drafts):
- Incident taxonomy v1: /eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-taxonomy-v1
- Incident metadata standard: /architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/incident-metadata-standard

Answers inline:

1) Required at declare vs post-incident
- At declaration: severity (existing), short title, primary category (taxonomy v1), impacted surface (choose one), region, and “primary owner team” (can be auto-suggested).
- Within 15 min: contributing factor (optional in v1 but strongly encouraged if obvious), customer tier (Hosted self-serve vs enterprise; Dedicated), and affected deployment mode.
- Post-incident: you can refine category (reclass) + add contributing factors + impacted service(s).

2) Allowed values enforcement
Incident-bot will enforce allowed values and write normalized tags. Console should consume and display the normalized values. If you need to allow editing in Console, we should keep it read-only for v1 (or edits should go through the same validation layer).

3) Impacted surface
In v1 we’re trying to keep “impacted surface” to one field w/ allowed values (customer-facing surface) + a separate optional field for technical “impacted service/component.” During an active incident, responders can usually pick customer-facing surface more reliably.

4) Minimal identifiers
Yes to:
- incident ID
- Slack channel (or link)
- postmortem link (if exists)
- status page incident link (optional, only when customer-visible)

We should also include “customer communication required: yes/no” as a metadata flag (Support requested).

If you can share a quick mock of the UI filters you’re planning, I can have Miles/Rafael sanity check the field list against what responders can actually provide under load.

-Neha


---

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 11:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting

Adding Support/CS lens.

For internal tooling (Console + reporting), the fields that most reduce back-and-forth during escalations:
- Customer tier + whether the incident is Dedicated (and which pool/region)
- “Customer comms required” + comms status (draft/sent/next update ETA)
- Primary owner team + escalation channel (even if Console only displays it)
- Links: Jira SUP ticket(s) / escalation thread (optional but huge for audit)

Strong preference that Console shows a “last updated” timestamp + who updated the incident metadata (even if edits only happen via incident-bot). During an incident, Support needs to know whether fields are stale vs actively maintained.

If there’s a v1 constraint to keep it light, I’d still push for:
- Comms required (Y/N)
- Next customer update ETA (freeform timestamp)

Thanks,
Dev
Customer Support Escalations


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 2:14 PM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting

This helps.

Proposed Console v1 approach (to keep us aligned with incident-bot + avoid creating a second editor):
- Read-only incident metadata view pulling from incident-bot normalized fields
- Filters: severity, primary category, impacted surface, owner team, region, deployment mode, customer tier
- Table columns: incident ID, title, status, start time, last updated, category, owner, region, TTM/TTR (as it becomes available), comms required
- Links out: Slack incident channel + postmortem doc (when present)

On editing: agree we should not edit taxonomy fields in Console for v1.

Open item: “customer tier” values — should we use the same tiers Support uses today (Self-serve / Growth / Enterprise) or map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? I worry we’ll conflate packaging vs deployment mode.

Neha — can you confirm preferred tier list for incident metadata? If you want, I can draft the exact field names + allowed values we’ll hardcode into filters for v1 and send for review.

-Marissa


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 4:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: fields needed for Console ops dashboard + reporting

Tier list: keep it simple in metadata.

Recommendation for v1:
- deployment_mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private (Redwood-operated)
- customer_tier: Self-serve | Enterprise

Rationale: packaging nuance isn’t worth the confusion for incident response + dashboards. Dedicated is primarily a deployment mode + operational surface; enterprise-ness is a comms/SLA driver.

If Product wants more granularity later, we can add an optional “account_segment” field, but not required.

If you send the field names + allowed values you plan to implement in Console filters, Rafael can confirm it matches incident-bot/ingestion and we’ll sign off in the taxonomy rollout checklist.

-Neha
